name: M23/RDF Seize Goma, Capital of North Kivu
target: Goma, provincial capital of North Kivu (pop. ~2 million)
casualties: Hundreds killed; 21 civilians executed in Kasika neighborhood
description: M23 rebels backed by Rwandan forces seized Goma after cutting all road connections by January 23. The city of 2 million became sealed under rebel control, triggering the world's largest displacement crisis.

name: M23 Captures Bukavu, South Kivu Capital
target: Bukavu, provincial capital of South Kivu, and Kavumu airport
description: After capturing Goma, M23 pushed south and seized Bukavu, the capital of South Kivu, including the strategic Kavumu airport. M23 established parallel administration in both provincial capitals.

name: Doha Framework for Peace Agreement Signed
target: Ceasefire and comprehensive peace framework
description: DRC government and AFC/M23 signed the Doha Framework establishing a ceasefire and terms for comprehensive peace negotiations mediated by Qatar.

name: Washington Peace Accords: Trump Brokers DRC-Rwanda Deal
target: US-brokered bilateral peace framework tying investment to security
description: President Trump brokered the Washington Accords between DRC and Rwanda, tying US investment to security stabilization and incentivizing alignment of national interests.

name: M23 Withdraws from Uvira; Post-Withdrawal Violence
target: City of Uvira, strategic Lake Tanganyika port
casualties: Post-withdrawal killings, looting, and sexual violence reported
description: M23 completed withdrawal from Uvira, placing the city under international community responsibility. FARDC reestablished control January 18-19, but a security vacuum caused immediate violence against civilians including killings, looting, and sexual assault.

name: Kamikaze Drone Attacks on Kisangani Airport
target: Bangboka International Airport, Kisangani (FARDC logistics hub)
description: M23/RDF launched kamikaze drone attacks on Kisangani's Bangboka International Airport, over 500km from M23-held territory. This marked a significant escalation in the conflict's technological dimension. Eight drones were intercepted.

name: Doha Ceasefire Monitoring Mechanism Signed
target: Ceasefire verification and monitoring structures
description: DRC government and AFC-M23 signed the mandate establishing the Ceasefire Monitoring and Verification Mechanism under the Doha Framework, creating formal structures to observe and report ceasefire compliance.

name: US Sanctions Entire Rwandan Defence Force
target: RDF (entire army) plus 4 senior officials including army chief of staff
description: US Treasury OFAC sanctioned the entire Rwandan Defence Force and four senior military officials for supporting M23 in violation of the Washington Accords. US State Department added visa restrictions on senior Rwandan officials on March 6.

name: Drone Strike on Goma Kills UNICEF Specialist
target: Residential area in Goma's Himbi neighborhood
casualties: 3 killed including UNICEF specialist Karine Buisset
description: Drone strikes hit Goma's Himbi quarter, killing three people including UNICEF specialist Karine Buisset. The strike on a residential area with an international aid worker drew widespread international condemnation.

name: Turkish Drone Strike on FARDC Position near Bijombo
target: DRC coalition military position in Bijombo highlands
casualties: Senior FARDC colonel and 5 soldiers killed in preceding ground attack
description: Rwanda reportedly conducted an airstrike using a Turkish-made medium-altitude long-endurance drone on a DRC coalition position in the Bijombo highlands. The strike followed a ground attack by Twirwaneho fighters that killed a senior FARDC colonel and five soldiers.

name: Montreux Talks: Prisoner Exchange Memorandum
target: Transfer of 2,000-3,000 FARDC soldiers and EJVM expansion
description: Under the Doha process, DRC and M23 signed a memorandum in Montreux on transferring 2,000-3,000 captured FARDC soldiers and expanding the joint verification mechanism to include M23 representatives.

name: US Sanctions M23 Intel Chief and Gold Smugglers
target: M23 intelligence chief John Imani Nzenze; Gasabo Gold Refinery and 3 mining companies (Jun 25)
description: US Treasury sanctioned M23's intelligence chief and an FDLR commander. On June 25, Treasury sanctioned the Gasabo Gold Refinery and three mining companies for smuggling minerals from DRC to Rwanda, targeting the conflict's economic engine.

name: M23 Offensive Captures Masisi Territory
target: Remeka (Aug 20) and Katoyi-center (Aug 25) in Masisi territory
description: M23 launched a multi-axis offensive in August, capturing Remeka and Katoyi-center in Masisi territory. A drone strike also hit the Mwalu Hotel in Fizi targeting military officials. DRC coalition shot down an Antonov cargo aircraft near Gahwela on August 27. Update: Remeka changed hands three times afterwards (FARDC 15 Sep, M23 25 Sep, FARDC 3 Oct); southern Masisi remained contested as of 13 Oct.

name: DRC-M23 Peace Roadmap Agreed in Geneva
target: Structured roadmap for Doha Framework negotiations
description: After talks August 17-21, DRC and M23 agreed to a structured roadmap defining stages and timetable for negotiations under the Doha Framework. Ceasefire verification mechanisms were standardized and EJVM+ deployed its first reconnaissance mission to Minembwe. Update: the ceasefire is not holding — the FARDC accused M23 and Rwanda of violations in Masisi and Walikale on 22 Sep, and the AU panel called on all sides to respect it on 7 Oct.

name: M23 Retakes Mitimingi, Claims Most of Katoyi
target: Mitimingi and Katoyi groupement, western Masisi
description: M23 retook Mitimingi and said it now held most of Katoyi, extending its August offensive toward the Walikale border. Wazalendo tried and failed to retake Mitimingi on Sep 22, but pro-government forces claimed it again on Oct 5. Approximate coordinates.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 4 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-4-2026
CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 25 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-25-2026

name: Government Coalition Drone-Backed Push on Minembwe
target: Twirwaneho (M23-allied) positions around Minembwe and Point Zero, South Kivu highlands
casualties: FARDC claimed 15 Twirwaneho killed (Aug 31) and 23 rebels (Sep 1); mass displacement
description: The FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian troops used drones, mortars and heavy weapons to retake Malimba, Rubarati, Masango and other villages south of Minembwe. Strikes on Point Zero, Mukoko and Nyaruhinga drove mass displacement. The front ground on through September and early October, with one-way attack drones used by both sides, including Twirwaneho drone strikes on Mulima and Gipimo.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 4 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-4-2026

name: M23 Takes Minjenje on Walikale Axis
target: Minjenje, Walikale territory (RP1030 axis)
description: M23 captured Minjenje after clashes with the FARDC and Wazalendo, during the same week the EJVM+ was verifying the ceasefire in Masisi. Government forces regained it on Sep 15 and pushed M23 back toward Malemo. It is one of several towns that changed hands repeatedly on the Masisi-Walikale line. Approximate coordinates.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 11 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-11-2026
CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 18 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-18-2026

name: EJVM+ Ceasefire Verification Mission to Masisi
target: Ceasefire compliance in Masisi territory
description: The expanded Joint Verification Mechanism ran a ceasefire verification field mission in Masisi from Sep 10 to 12, its second after Minembwe in late August. The ICGLR issued a statement on Sep 20. MONUSCO chief James Swan met M23 and EJVM+ in Goma on Sep 21–22, and FARDC and M23 officers held a working session under the EJVM+ on Sep 24. Fighting continued throughout.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 25 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-25-2026

name: Rwanda-Almonty Tungsten Deal Under Washington Track
target: Rwandan tungsten development
description: Rwanda and the US-Canadian miner Almonty agreed to develop tungsten, with Rwanda taking a 25% stake in a new subsidiary. The State Department said it helped facilitate the deal under the US-Rwanda framework and the Regional Economic Integration Framework of the Washington Peace Accords. It is the first concrete minerals deal on the Rwanda side of the accords.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 18 2026 (citing Bloomberg, Reuters, BusinessWire) — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-18-2026

name: FARDC-Wazalendo Push Takes Remeka, Nears Ngungu
target: Miko hill, Remeka, Kasake, Muhororo, southern Masisi
description: The FARDC and Wazalendo, reportedly with FDLR and Nyatura fighters, took Miko hill and Remeka on Sep 15. They claimed Katuunda, Kaleta, Muhororo and Kasake on Sep 16 and pressed toward Ngungu. This reversed M23's August gains in southern Masisi and was the largest government advance since the Doha roadmap. Approximate coordinates.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 18 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-18-2026
CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 25 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-25-2026

name: M23 Foils Plot to Oust Military Chief Makenga
target: AFC/M23 military leadership
description: Africa Intelligence reported that M23 had thwarted a plot to remove military chief Sultani Makenga. The plot was allegedly led by Theo Binamungu, an adviser to Corneille Nangaa arrested in late August, and was reportedly presented to members of Rwanda's security apparatus. It is the first reported internal split at the top of the movement.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Sep 25 2026 (citing Africa Intelligence) — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/september-25-2026

name: M23 Recaptures Remeka, Nkokwe and Muhororo
target: Remeka, Nkokwe, Muhororo, southern Masisi
description: M23 counterattacked and retook the southern Masisi villages lost on Sep 15–16. The FARDC and Wazalendo claimed them again on Oct 3 along with Kamuhobe, Nyamiri and Mihano, and M23 retook Numbi, Shanje and Kavumu on Oct 7. This Remeka seesaw is the clearest sign that the Doha ceasefire is not holding in Masisi. Approximate coordinates.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Oct 7 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/october-7-2026

name: Twirwaneho and RED-Tabara Seize Mwenga Villages
target: Magunda, Maheta, Kakuku, Mushojo, Nanjale, Mwenga territory
description: The M23-allied Twirwaneho, reportedly with the Burundian rebel group RED-Tabara, captured five villages in Mwenga, northwest of the Minembwe front. The reported presence of RED-Tabara draws Burundi's own insurgency into the South Kivu highlands fight. Approximate coordinates.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Oct 7 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/october-7-2026

name: First Drone Strike on Pinga Airfield; DRC Blames Rwanda
target: FARDC position at Pinga airfield, Walikale territory
description: A drone attack hit the FARDC position at Pinga airfield, the government's Walikale logistics hub. CTP calls it the first reported M23 air attack on the town. On Sep 29 the DRC's UN representative told the Security Council that Rwanda was responsible and had used a Turkish-made TB2-type drone. Pro-government forces said they shot down a drone over Rugezi the same day.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Oct 7 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/october-7-2026

name: Burundi Bans Entry From M23-Held Areas
target: Border entry for people coming from M23-held territory, including UN personnel
description: Burundi's interior minister banned entry for people arriving from M23-held areas, including UN personnel. This hardened Burundi's front-line role alongside its troops fighting in the South Kivu highlands. Separately, the same day DRC envoys Anzuluni and Sita Mambu met President Ndayishimiye in Bujumbura on a regional tour.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Oct 7 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/october-7-2026

name: AU Panel Meets M23 in Goma, Kagame in Kigali
target: Revival of ceasefire and Doha engagement
description: AU facilitators Uhuru Kenyatta, Mokgweetsi Masisi and Sahle-Work Zewde met AFC/M23 leadership in Goma on Oct 5, then MONUSCO, OCHA, ICRC and the EJVM+. Kenyatta met Rwanda's foreign minister on Oct 6. On Oct 7 the panel met Kagame and urged all sides to respect the ceasefire and resume the Doha process, while fighting continued in Masisi and Kalehe.
sources: CTP Congo War Security Review, Oct 7 2026 — https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/october-7-2026
